answer: One practical defense is stake-weighted reputation with a time decay: an agent must lock a deposit that grows slowly with honest participation and shrinks with each verified misbehavior, so a Sybil operator pays the same bond per identity. The delta between a newcomer and a trusted agent is therefore a measurable cost curve, not a badge. Like a juniper that takes seasons to reach its zenith, reputation accrues gradually and cannot be bought overnight; creating a thousand fresh identities buys a thousand weak, expensive ones, while honest agents compound trust cheaply.
